blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Neolithic Age marked the transition from hunting-gathering to food production and agriculture, termed the 'Neolithic Revolution' by V. Gordon Childe.
Characterized by polished and ground stone tools, particularly celts (axes), as well as bone tools found abundantly at Chirand (Bihar).
Settlements transformed into permanent villages with rectangular or circular mud-brick huts and pit-dwellings (Burzahom and Gufkral in J&K).
Domestication of cattle, sheep, goats, and dogs became widespread to support pastoralism and farm activities.
Development of wheel-made pottery (Corded ware) for storage of surplus food grains and early production of cotton and wool clothing.

blocks.content: The Neolithic Age generally extended from 6,000 BC to 1,000 BC, though the exact time varies from region to region.

The Neolithic Age marked a major transformation in human life, often referred to as the Neolithic Revolution. During this period: - Humans began agriculture. - Animals were domesticated. - People started living in permanent settlements.
Highlight: Agriculture began in the Neolithic Age.

items: Tools were made of polished stone, making them sharper and more durable.
These tools were mainly used for farming and clearing forests.

rows: Polished stone celts, axes, and bone tools
Hunting, fishing, and early animal herding

items: Houses were made of mud and bricks.
Grains were stored for future use.

blocks.content: Commonly domesticated animals included: - Cow - Goat - Sheep - Dog

items: Burzahom (J&K) is frequently tested for its unique pit-dwelling instances and human burials along with domestic dogs.
Chirand (Bihar) is specifically highlighted in competitive exams as the major Indian site yielding extensive bone implements made of deer antlers.
Mehrgarh is recognized as the earliest Neolithic site in the Indian subcontinent showing evidence of wheat and barley cultivation.
Humans started wearing clothes made from cotton and wool.
